name: Darlughdacha

attributes.name: Darlughdacha
attributes.attribute: burned her feet, healed by Brigit

sources: Condren, Mary. The Serpent and the Goddess: Women, Religion and Power in Ancient Ireland. San Francisco: Harper & Row, 1989, 71.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Darlughdacha was an Irish heroine. Her name is also written Darludacha. It means daughter of the god Lugh. When the goddess Brigit became a saint, monks gave her a human life story. They made her abbess of Kildare. Darlughdacha was Brigit's boon companion. The two shared a bed. Darlughdacha burned her feet to mortify the flesh. She had gazed lustfully at a warrior. Brigit healed her feet. A historical woman of this name may have existed. More likely she was a lost Celtic goddess. Interpreters recast her as a Christian nun.
objective: This record documents Darlughdacha, the companion of Saint Brigit, possibly a lost Celtic goddess recast as a nun.
key_results: Darlughdacha means daughter of the god Lugh.
Brigit was made abbess of Kildare when she became a saint.
Scholars read Darlughdacha as a lost Celtic goddess turned nun.
